reviews.comment: I had Dr. Pappas for PHIL 205. I loved him as a professor and I loved his class. He had one midterm essay, one final essay, two 1-page class-reflection essays, and an occasional in-class one-question quiz. His class is incredible do-able and it is easy to follow. There are weekly outside readings, but they are very interesting and not too long.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's very passionate about what he teaches. If I would have cared more about the class, I would have enjoyed him more. He is really funny and lectures very passionately. There are 2 essays, 2 critical reflections, and a pop quiz once a week. Not an easy A, but very manageable if you work!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Pappas is a straight forward man. He lectures passionately, so be ready to discuss the readings. He outlines the major essays clearly as well as the reflections. Not many assignments, but a lot of reading and a weekly quiz. Simple things. He's intimidating at first, at least to me, but he's a cool man. Would totally take him again.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor does not use ecampus and does not upload grades so you are unsure on what grade you received in the class. There are better and worse philosophy teachers but if you want to know how you stand in the class grade-wise you will need to go to his office.

Dr. Pappas is a phenomenal being. I have taken two classes with him and I am sad that the semester has come to an end. Grading criteria is straightforward. Reading heavy. Challenging discussions, but also very rewarding. I recommend Dr. Pappas 1000%. He is an ideal Professor and I will remember him for the rest of my life.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Pappas has been my favorite professor in college. He has engaging lectures and truly wants you to learn in his classes.

Pappas' class is a class you wanted to go to. It was the highlight of my week attending his lectures. Yahoo group centered discussions and overall very enjoyable. Currently taking his Philosophy 415 class. As a philosophy major he is overall my favorite Prof on campus.

For Latin American Philosophy Dr. Pappas makes the class pretty interesting. The second half of the class isn't as intersting as the first, but the ease of the class stays the same. There are only two tests and four mini opinion pieces. It's pretty hard to fail this class, everything is straightforward.
